summary: Kodo Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and held a post as a researcher at Taisho University.

Scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy Kodo Sawaki studied under Koho Sawada, Zenko Sawada, Ryo-un Fueoka, Join Saeki, and Sotan Oka at institutions including Senju-ji and Horyuji Kangakuin. He served as professor at Komazawa University and abbot of Antai-ji.
Kodo Yamada was a Buddhist studies scholar who held teaching positions at Komazawa University and Keio University.
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Kodo Yotsuya earned an MA at Komazawa University under Shiro Matsumoto and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg.
Koen Wellens works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Charles Willemen at Ghent University and completed a PhD at the University of Oslo supervised by Per Kværne.
Koenraad Elst is a scholar of Indology, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at KU Leuven, earning an MA, and also studied at Banaras Hindu University.

Kogen Mizuno studied Indology and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo, receiving a Doctorate of Letters. He served as professor and president of Komazawa University, professor at the University of Tokyo, and president of Iwamizawa Komazawa Junior College.
Koichi Hiraoka specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Waseda University, he served as a visiting professor at Shuchiin University.

Koichi Hokazono, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at the University of Bonn and earned a PhD from Kyushu University. He held posts at Kagoshima International University and Kyushu University.

Koichi Shinohara is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He was a professor at McMaster University, coordinator of the Numata Program at the University of Toronto Mississauga, and a senior lecturer at Yale University.

Koichi Takahashi, an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, completed his PhD at the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima and Akira Saito. He later served as assistant, project researcher, and professor at the University of Tokyo.

Koichi Yokoyama studied Buddhist studies and philosophy at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and traditional teacher Gyōin Hashimoto. He later served as an assistant professor at Rikkyo University.
Buddhist studies scholar Koin Takada studied at Ryukoku University and under Gyōin Hashimoto, whom he succeeded in 1967.

Koji Kamioka studied linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies at Kyoto University under Yutaka Ochihara. He served as a lecturer at Kyoto Sangyo University and as a member at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
Koji Shindo studied Buddhist studies as a graduate student at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies and worked as a part-time lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University.
Koji Takahashi studied at Otani University and earned a literature doctorate from Bukkyo University, where he also served as an assistant professor and professor of Buddhist studies.
Sinologist Kojiro Yoshikawa studied at Kyoto University and served there as Professor of Chinese Language and Literature, later serving as chairman of the board at Toho Gakkai.

Kojun Fukui, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, studied under Sokichi Tsuda at Waseda University, where he earned a doctorate and served as professor. He was also president of Taisho University and founded the Society of Taoistic Research.
Kojun Saito, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied under Seiren Matsunami and served as a lecturer at Taisho University.
Kokan Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yujun Endo and served as a professor at Koyasan University.
